headline: DA Backs Industry’s Proposed ₱210/Kilo Hog Floor Price but Says It Cannot Mandate It
seoTitle: DA Backs ₱210/Kilo Hog Floor Price Proposal, Says It Lacks Legal Authority | FMB News
seoDescription: The Department of Agriculture supports the hog industry’s proposed ₱210-per-kilo live-hog floor price but says current law does not allow it to impose the price as mandatory.
deck: Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. says the ₱210 figure came from the hog industry and has DA support, but the department currently lacks legal authority to impose a mandatory floor price.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of Agriculture said Sunday that it supports the hog industry’s proposal for a ₱210-per-kilo floor price for live hogs as farmgate prices in some areas fall to between ₱120 and ₱160 per kilo.
Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. stressed that the ₱210 figure was proposed by industry, not by the department.

sections.heading: What the DA can and cannot do
paragraphs: The DA says it currently has no legal authority to impose a mandatory farmgate floor price. The ₱210 figure is therefore a policy target supported by the department, not an enforceable nationwide price.
Tiu Laurel said the department is discussing other measures with economic managers, including restoring previous pork tariff rates and considering higher special safeguard duties.

sections.heading: What else the department is doing
paragraphs: The DA said it is tightening checks on imported meat handling in public markets through the National Meat Inspection Service and is monitoring meat prices ahead of the Christmas season.
The department expects seasonal demand to push prices higher but says it prefers any increase to remain limited.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The proposal reflects pressure on hog producers from low farmgate prices while consumers continue to face much higher retail pork prices. Any eventual government intervention would need to balance producer viability, food inflation and legal constraints.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for any formal tariff or safeguard-duty action, new legislation or executive steps that could give the government an enforceable mechanism, and whether farmgate prices recover without a mandatory floor.

verificationNotes: The Department of Agriculture’s September 20 official release confirms support for the industry-proposed ₱210-per-kilo live-hog floor price and explicitly states that the DA currently lacks legal authority to impose it.
GMA News independently reported the DA statement and the current farmgate-price range cited by the department.
Philstar previously reported the industry proposal and the DA’s legal limitation, providing background rather than being treated as a new September 20 event.
The article distinguishes DA support from an enforceable price rule.
The contextual piggery photograph was taken in San Narciso, Zambales by Kuya Frank and is licensed CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.
